{{Short description|German supercomputer company}}
'''SciEngines GmbH''' is a privately owned company founded 2007 as a spin-off of the COPACOBANA<ref>{{cite web | title = COPACOBANA Project | url = https://www.sciengines.com/copacobana/about.html }}</ref> project by the [[Ruhr University|Universities of Bochum]] and [[University of Kiel|Kiel]], both in [[Germany]]. The project intended to create a platform for an affordable [[Custom hardware attack]]. COPACOBANA<ref>{{cite web | title = COPACOBANA: FPGA based DES Cracker | url = https://jchblue.blogspot.com/2009/08/copacobana-fpga-based-des-cracker.html | date = 2009-08-16 }}</ref> is a massively-parallel [[Reconfigurable computing|reconfigurable computer]]. It can be utilized to perform a so-called [[Brute force attack]] to recover DES<ref>{{cite web | title = SHARCS Workshop, April 3.- 4., 2006, Cologne, How to Break DES for € 8,980 | url = https://www.hyperelliptic.org/tanja/SHARCS/talks06/copacobana.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = COPACOBANA in german computer magazine c't | url = http://www.sciengines.com/company/news-a-events/77-copacobana-in-ct.html }}</ref> encrypted data.  It consists of 120 commercially available, reconfigurable integrated circuits ([[FPGA]]s). These [[Xilinx]] Spartan3-1000 run in parallel, and create a massively parallel system.  Since 2007, SciEngines GmbH has enhanced and developed successors of COPACOBANA. Furthermore, the COPACOBANA has become a well known reference platform for [[cryptanalysis]] and  [[Custom hardware attack|custom hardware]] based attacks to symmetric, asymmetric cyphers and stream ciphers. 2008 attacks against [[Stream cipher|A5/1 stream cipher]] an encryption system been used to encrypt voice streams in [[GSM]] have been published as the first known real world attack utilizing off-the-shelf custom hardware.<ref>{{cite web | title = A Real-World Attack Breaking A5/1 within Hours | url = http://www.emsec.rub.de/media/crypto/attachments/files/2010/05/ches2008_breaking_a51_within_hours.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Hardware-Based Cryptanalysis of the GSM A5/1 Encryption Algorithm | url = http://www.emsec.rub.de/media/crypto/attachments/files/2010/04/da_gendrullis.pdf }}</ref>

They introduced in 2008 their RIVYERA S3-5000<ref>{{cite web | title = RIVYERA from SciEngines | url = http://superconductor.voltage.com/2010/06/rivyera-from-sciengines.html }}</ref> enhancing the performance of the computer dramatically via using 128 Spartan-3 5000's. Currently SciEngines RIVYERA holds the record in brute-force breaking DES utilizing 128 Spartan-3 5000 FPGAs.<ref>{{Cite press release | url = http://www.sciengines.com/company/news-a-events/74-des-in-1-day.html | title = Break DES in less than a single day }} Demonstrated at 2009 Workshop.</ref>  Current systems provide a unique density of up to 256 Spartan-6 FPGAs per single system enabling scientific utilization beyond the field of cryptanalysis, like [[bioinformatics]].<ref>{{cite journal | title = Vy-PER: eliminating false positive detection of virus integration events in next generation sequencing data | date = 2015 | doi = 10.1038/srep11534  | doi-access = free| last1 = Forster | first1 = Michael | last2 = Szymczak | first2 = Silke | last3 = Ellinghaus | first3 = David | last4 = Hemmrich | first4 = Georg | last5 = Rühlemann | first5 = Malte | last6 = Kraemer | first6 = Lars | last7 = Mucha | first7 = Sören | last8 = Wienbrandt | first8 = Lars | last9 = Stanulla | first9 = Martin | last10 = Franke | first10 = Andre | last11 = Franke | first11 = A. | journal = Scientific Reports | volume = 5 | article-number = 11534 | pmid = 26166306 | pmc = 4499804 | bibcode = 2015NatSR...511534. }}</ref>

:2006 original developers of the COPACOBANA<ref>{{cite web | title = COPACOBANA: FPGA based DES Cracker | url = https://jchblue.blogspot.com/2009/08/copacobana-fpga-based-des-cracker.html | date = 2009-08-16 }}</ref> form the company
:2007 introduction of the COPACOBANA (Copacobana S3-1000) as a [COTS]
:2007 first demonstration of COPACOBANA 5000<ref>{{cite web | title = RIVYERA from SciEngines | url = http://ww2.cs.mu.oz.au/~schroder/pbss_iccs09.pdf}}</ref>
:2008 they introduced RIVYERA S3-5000, the direct successor of COPACOBANA 5000 and COPACOBANA. The RIVYERA architecture introduced a new high performance optimized bus system and a fully [[API]] encapsulated communication framework.
:2008 demonstration of the COPACOBANA V4-SX35, a 128 Virtex-4 SX35 FPGA cluster (COPACOBANA shared bus architecture)
:2008 introduction of the RIVYERA V4-SX35, a 128 Virtex-4 SX35 FPGA cluster (RIVYERA [[High-performance computing|HPC]] architecture)
:2009 they introduced RIVYERA S6-LX150.
:2011 they introduced 256 User usable FPGAs per RIVYERA S6-LX150 computer.


Providing a standard off-the-shelf [[Intel]] CPU and mainboard integrated into the FPGA computer RIVYERA<ref>{{cite web | title = HOCHLEISTUNGSCLUSTER RIVYER | url = https://www.ei.rub.de/fakultaet/banner/rivyera/ }}</ref> systems allow to execute most standard code without modifications. SciEngines aims that programmers only have to focus on porting the most time-consuming 5% of their code to the FPGA. Therefore, they bundle an [[Eclipse (software)|Eclipse]] like development environment which allows code implementation in hardware based implementation languages e.g. [[VHDL]], [[Verilog]] as well as in [[C (programming language)|C]] based languages. An [[Application Programming Interface]] in C, [[C++]], [[Java (programming language)|Java]] and [[Fortran]] allow scientists and programmers to adopt their code to benefit from an application-specific hardware architecture.
